task_instance: Synthesize a small onboarding-research corpus (6 interview notes covering solo/mid-market/enterprise users + a 96-response survey with open-ended coding and NPS cross-tabs) into a structured research synthesis: findings with evidence/frequency/impact/confidence, user segments, opportunity areas, prioritized recommendations, and open questions.
evidence: Created raw_inputs/interviews.md (6 synthetic interview notes across solo, mid-market, and enterprise segments) and raw_inputs/survey_results.md (96-response survey with Likert distribution, segment breakdown, coded open-ended themes, NPS, and an NPS cross-tab) inside the work directory. Performed the skill's actual workflow by hand: extracted observations/quotes/pain points per interview, cross-referenced against survey-coded themes (triangulation), built a frequency x impact view, and wrote synthesis.md containing all sections the skill specifies: Research Overview, 7 Key Findings (each with finding statement, evidence with attribution, frequency, impact, confidence level, ordered by priority), User Segments (3 evidence-based segments with size estimates), Opportunity Areas (4, prioritized), Recommendations (6, each tied to a specific finding and rated on impact/feasibility), and Open Questions (5, including explicit gaps like analytics not available in this research pass). Verified by checking the document's headers (grep '^#') confirm all required section levels are present and by rereading the content for internal consistency (e.g., the -8 vs +19 NPS cross-tab in the survey data is correctly reflected as the primary quantitative support for Finding 2). No connectors, credentials, or external services were needed -- this skill's core deliverable is a pure text-synthesis/writing task achievable with only file read/write, which the developer-sandbox runtime fully supports.
